headline: 6-year-old missing child’s body found in sack in Bogura
summary: The girl was strangled to death; police suspect she was killed for her gold earrings. Four people, including a neighbor, have been arrested.
details: Police recovered the body of six-year-old Rakika Akter Raka from a white plastic sack inside a house in Bogura’s Adamdighi upazila.
The girl had gone missing on Thursday afternoon while returning home from private tuition in the Malshan Sahebpara area of Santahar municipality.
The prime suspect, neighbor Amjad Hossain, and three others—his wife Bonna, friend Md Babu, and Babu’s wife Asha—have been arrested.
Police suspect the child was killed for her gold earrings, which were missing when her body was recovered.
An investigating officer stated that the victim was strangled to death, with an injury mark found on the left side of her head.
Following the discovery, local residents caught and assaulted the suspects before police arrived to rescue and take them into custody.
The suspects are currently being processed through the legal system, while the child's body has been handed over to her family after a post-mortem.
caption:
A 6-year-old girl was found dead in a sack in her neighbor's house. Police suspect she was killed for gold earrings.

Police recovered the body of six-year-old Rakika Akter Raka from a white plastic sack inside a house in Bogura’s Adamdighi upazila.

The girl had gone missing on Thursday afternoon while returning home from private tuition in the Malshan Sahebpara area of Santahar municipality.

The prime suspect, neighbor Amjad Hossain, and three others—his wife Bonna, friend Md Babu, and Babu’s wife Asha—have been arrested.

Police suspect the child was killed for her gold earrings, which were missing when her body was recovered.

An investigating officer stated that the victim was strangled to death, with an injury mark found on the left side of her head.

Following the discovery, local residents caught and assaulted the suspects before police arrived to rescue and take them into custody.

The suspects are currently being processed through the legal system, while the child's body has been handed over to her family after a post-mortem.

headline_marked: World Cup openers: [[Streaming platforms hit by disruptions]] in Bangladesh
headline: World Cup openers: Streaming platforms hit by disruptions in Bangladesh
summary: Fans report buffering, payment issues, and login failures on Toffee and Bioscope+ during the opening matches of the 2026 FIFA World Cup.
details: Football fans across Bangladesh faced widespread disruptions while streaming the opening matches of the 2026 FIFA World Cup on June 12.
Users of Toffee, the Banglalink-operated platform, reported delayed one-time passwords (OTPs), payment problems, and frequent buffering during live broadcasts.
Banglalink's head of corporate communications, Gazi Towhid Ahmed, attributed the delays to an unusually high volume of OTP requests following an initial feed disruption.
Similarly, Bioscope+ users, operated by Grameenphone, reported technical problems, with some unable to log in and seeing only the app's loading animation.
Grameenphone's head of communications, Sharfuddin Ahmed Chowdhury, apologized for the inconvenience, stating that teams worked with priority to restore service.
Frustrated subscribers took to social media to demand refunds and question whether the platforms had invested enough in infrastructure to handle the surge in demand.
With the tournament progressing, attention now turns to whether providers can prevent similar outages as millions of viewers tune in for live coverage.
caption:
Paid for a subscription but stuck with a loading screen? World Cup fans in Bangladesh are furious.

Football fans across Bangladesh faced widespread disruptions while streaming the opening matches of the 2026 FIFA World Cup on June 12.

Users of Toffee, the Banglalink-operated platform, reported delayed one-time passwords (OTPs), payment problems, and frequent buffering during live broadcasts.

Banglalink's head of corporate communications, Gazi Towhid Ahmed, attributed the delays to an unusually high volume of OTP requests following an initial feed disruption.

Similarly, Bioscope+ users, operated by Grameenphone, reported technical problems, with some unable to log in and seeing only the app's loading animation.

Grameenphone's head of communications, Sharfuddin Ahmed Chowdhury, apologized for the inconvenience, stating that teams worked with priority to restore service.

Frustrated subscribers took to social media to demand refunds and question whether the platforms had invested enough in infrastructure to handle the surge in demand.

With the tournament progressing, attention now turns to whether providers can prevent similar outages as millions of viewers tune in for live coverage.

Source: The Daily Star, Prothom Alo
